title: The Lighter Brief
overview: A big civic week: Mary Peltola won Alaska's Senate race, and the White House pulled its FDA nominee. Closer to home for Charlotte readers, there were two tiny earthquakes, Duke Energy bills are going up, and Levine Children's Hospital has a big expansion planned. For the lighter side, Big Boi landed a 200-pound marlin and the whole internet is rooting for Fiona the hippo to pass a hat.

stories.headline: Two tiny earthquakes give Rowan and Iredell a jolt
stories.summary: Two small earthquakes, measured at 2.4 and 2.2, rumbled through the Rowan and Iredell County area late Tuesday and early Wednesday. Many people heard a loud boom more than they felt shaking, and some 911 callers thought it was an explosion. One Statesville resident said his sleeping dog jumped up and barked just before the house shook.
key_facts: One quake was a 2.4 near Cleveland in Rowan County; the other was a 2.2 in the Iredell County area
The Iredell quake hit at 11:05 p.m. Tuesday, about 1 km below the surface
USGS first listed the Iredell quake at 2.4, then revised it to 2.2
North Carolina's biggest quake in 100 years was a 5.1 near Sparta in 2020
stories.why: No damage or injuries were reported, and now you know what that mystery boom was.

stories.headline: Mary Peltola wins Alaska's Senate race and makes history
stories.summary: Two weeks after Election Day, the AP called Alaska's Senate race for Democrat Mary Peltola over Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan. Peltola, who is Yup'ik, becomes the first Alaska Native elected to the U.S. Senate. The win gives Democrats 56 Senate seats, and they also won back the House. A federal investigation is still under way into whether a lesser-known candidate with a similar name was recruited to pull votes from the incumbent.
key_facts: Unofficial results: Peltola 50.12%, Sullivan 45.80%
Democrats gained nine Senate seats in the midterms
Alaska plans to certify the results on November 25
Peltola is the first Democrat to win a U.S. Senate seat in Alaska since 2008
disputed: The DOJ probe asks whether Democrats recruited Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. as a spoiler candidate. Peltola, the DSCC and Sullivan Jr. all deny this.
Fox News Digital reported more than 200 subpoenas. Newsweek has not independently confirmed that number.
The results are unofficial until the state certifies them.
stories.why: The result shapes who controls Congress for the last two years of Trump's term, and it marks a historic first for Alaska Native representation.

stories.headline: White House withdraws its pick to lead the FDA
stories.summary: The White House pulled Heidi Overton's nomination for FDA commissioner just hours before a planned Senate committee vote. Her September hearing had drawn questions from both parties. Sen. Bill Cassidy, the Republican who chairs the committee, called the move 'odd' and said he believed she had a viable path to confirmation. Since May, the FDA has been led by an interim chief, Kyle Diamantas.
key_facts: The committee vote had been planned for Nov. 18
Former commissioner Marty Makary left the FDA in May
Citi analysts called the withdrawal a 'modest sentiment negative' but not a big near-term change for drug regulation
Sen. Roger Marshall has been discussed as a possible replacement, per Semafor
stories.why: The FDA approves medicines and keeps food safe, so who leads it affects almost everyone, though analysts don't expect day-to-day disruption.

stories.headline: Duke Energy bills in North Carolina will rise starting in January
stories.summary: The North Carolina Utilities Commission approved a 9.5% Duke Energy rate increase phased in over two years, starting Jan. 1, 2027. Some customers say their budgets are already stretched.
key_facts: 9.5% total increase over two years
Higher rates begin Jan. 1, 2027
stories.why: With a little notice, you can plan your budget ahead of the January change.

stories.headline: State gives Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools an 11-step plan to rebuild trust
stories.summary: The North Carolina State Board of Education sent the CMS school board a letter laying out 11 steps it expects the board to take to rebuild public trust. The letter comes while several investigations into the district are under way. State leaders say the steps will strengthen how the district is run.
key_facts: 11 expectations were sent to CMS Board Chair Gregory 'Dee' Rankin
A new CMS strategy committee has met since the letter arrived
stories.why: How CMS responds could affect how one of the state's largest school districts is governed.

stories.headline: Reggae Boyz exit the Nations League, but the coach sees progress
stories.summary: Jamaica lost 1-0 at Mexico, which tied the quarter-final 3-3 on aggregate, and Mexico went through on away goals. Head coach Rudolph Speed said the team has found an identity and will get stronger once injured players return. Defender Ronaldo Webster said they'll keep improving 'window by window.'
key_facts: Jamaica had led 3-2 going into the second leg
Jesús Corona scored Mexico's goal in the first half
Jamaica now heads to the Gold Cup qualification play-offs
stories.why: It's a close loss to a team ranked 10th in the world, and there's still a Gold Cup path ahead.

links.title: Speed: Boyz moving in right direction despite Nations League exit

stories.headline: Travis Scott-linked company drops its claim on the Houston Comets name
stories.summary: TSTM Holdings, a company tied to Travis Scott, abandoned its application to trademark the 'Houston Comets' name. That clears the way for the WNBA, which is bringing the Comets back next season after the Connecticut Sun moves to Houston. The new Comets logos were unveiled the same day.
key_facts: The application was abandoned Oct. 29, 2026, and terminated by the USPTO on Oct. 30
TSTM first filed in May 2024
The original Comets won the WNBA's first four championships before folding in 2008
disputed: Confirmed: USPTO records show the application was abandoned.
Scott's link to TSTM comes from reporting (a source cited by Chron and a shared attorney). Delaware LLCs don't have to name their members.
It's unclear whether there was a settlement or Scott's side simply dropped it.
stories.why: A classic WNBA name is coming home to Houston without a legal fight.

stories.headline: Levine Children's Hospital plans a $387 million expansion
stories.summary: Atrium Health announced its largest-ever investment in Levine Children's Hospital in Charlotte. The plan adds more than 100 pediatric beds and more than doubles both the emergency department and the surgery space. Demand has climbed 43% in five years, and the hospital already serves kids from 96 of North Carolina's 100 counties.
key_facts: The expansion brings the hospital to roughly 350 beds
It adds more than 40 NICU beds
Construction is expected to start in 2027 and will happen in phases
It includes a dedicated pediatric imaging center
stories.why: More families will be able to get specialized care for their kids close to home.
